open_points.subject: 50_public_apis.md:public_op:runtime_settings.load_runtime_settings
open_points.text: A missing, malformed or inconsistent value (a wildcard host or origin, binary bounds out of order) is refused with the `ValueError` the emitted `runtime_settings` raises, never carrying a value
open_points.question: Must the ValueError identify the offending environment variable, and if so by what stable field or message format?
options: Identify the variable by name in the message
Identify it in a structured exception field
open_points.default_guess: Use one built-in ValueError whose message names the variable but never includes its raw value.

open_points.subject: 50_public_apis.md:public_op:runtime_settings.load_runtime_settings
open_points.text: A missing, malformed or inconsistent value (a wildcard host or origin, binary bounds out of order) is refused with the `ValueError` the emitted `runtime_settings` raises, never carrying a value
open_points.question: May callers distinguish missing, malformed and inconsistent settings through exception subclasses, fields or messages, or must all causes have the same observable error shape?
options: One ValueError type with cause-specific messages
Distinct ValueError subclasses or structured cause fields
open_points.default_guess: Use the same ValueError type with no structured cause, while allowing a diagnostic message that identifies the variable.

open_points.subject: 50_public_apis.md:public_op:runtime_settings.load_runtime_settings
open_points.question: Which exception channels are forbidden from carrying the raw environment value: only the displayed message, or also args, attributes, repr, cause/context chaining and trace output?
options: Forbid the raw value in every exception channel
Forbid it only in the ValueError message and logs
Permit it in a chained internal exception
open_points.default_guess: Forbid the raw value in the exception message, args, attributes, repr and chained cause or context.

open_points.subject: 50_public_apis.md:public_op:runtime_settings.load_runtime_settings
open_points.text: A later call reads the same process environment the start validated, so it is not refused (State 3 Configuration); the emitted `binary_storage` would still answer such a refusal as `BinaryStorageError` (A14).
open_points.question: Can a post-start call to load_runtime_settings fail validation or not; if it can, what must registry_gateway and binary_storage each expose, and if it cannot, why is BinaryStorageError translation required?
options: Post-start validation failure is impossible; remove the hypothetical BinaryStorageError translation
Post-start failure is possible; binary_storage translates it and registry_gateway propagates ValueError
Post-start failure is possible; both callers translate it to their own boundary errors
open_points.default_guess: Treat every call as a fresh live-environment validation: binary_storage translates failure to BinaryStorageError and registry_gateway lets ValueError propagate.

open_points.subject: 50_public_apis.md:public_op:runtime_settings.load_runtime_settings
open_points.text: the emitted `binary_storage` would still answer such a refusal as `BinaryStorageError` (A14).
open_points.rule: note, которая не должна создавать ребро, не называет чужой экспорт целым словом
open_points.question: Rewrite the runtime_settings passage without naming the foreign export BinaryStorageError, and place binary_storage's translation behavior in the binary_storage operation that owns it.
